LESSON: TIME, DISTANCE AND SPEED

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurements
Topic 3.5: Time, Distance and Speed
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Time, Distance and Speed, part of Measurements in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: Why do we relate distance, time and speed? 2. How do we use speed in daily activities?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Use analog or digital clock to tell time in hours, minutes and seconds and discuss the units of time. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views.

2. Create conversion table on units of time. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional part of the body or use appropriate assistive devices to perform the task 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Use analog or digital clock to tell time in hours, minutes and seconds and discuss the units of time. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views.
2. Create conversion table on units of time. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional part of the body or use appropriate assistive devices to perform the task 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Time, Distance and Speed together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving: as the learner creates conversion tables relate and determine distance, time and speed.

● Self-efficacy: as the learner observes punctuality in attending to different activities.

Values

● Patriotism: as the learner observes road safety rules including speed limits for crossing the roads.

● Integrity: as the learner observes punctuality and work out correct distances.
